criteriaAssessment.counterevidence: All board write handlers inspected route through checkOrReplayProjectWriteReceipt before replay. criteriaAssessment.criterion: Receipt body retention and replay regression evidence
criteriaAssessment.counterevidence: The receipt sanitizer only retains identifiers/version/status markers and the existing board suite contains an active same-key replay and changed-body collision case. The board suite does not exercise grant removal/demotion replay, same-key concurrency, or inspect stored response_body for private content. The test suite could not execute in this review.

criteriaAssessment.criterion: BRD-07 cursor scope, filter, and ordering revision binding
criteriaAssessment.counterevidence: The continuation SQL stays constrained to the requested board and active cards, uses deterministic position/id ordering, and rejects malformed cursors. The cursor is not bound to board ID, query filters, or board/order revision, and the route does not verify snapshot/structure version. A card moved to a position before an existing cursor can be silently omitted; a cursor from another board or filter is accepted as a raw seek position. This violates the stale-cursor refresh contract.

security.reason: The previous replay-before-authorization flaw appears corrected in mounted board mutation paths: current grant and archive-context locks precede receipt access. No runtime regression suite ran, and reviewer identity IDs are unavailable.

correctness.reason: BRD-07 cursor does not detect stale board/order/filter context and can silently omit cards after ordering changes. Other board paths are statically implemented against the route set, but runtime acceptance was unavailable.

integrity.reason: Board and column writes use transactions, optimistic versions, constraints, and receipt serialization. Same-key race and stale-page integrity behavior are not evidenced by the requested suite.

tests.reason: Typecheck passed, but the required PostgreSQL suite failed before any test case; required receipt regressions and the broader frozen checks are absent or unrun.

maintainability.reason: Typed contracts, modular adapters, parameterized SQL, and a shared authorization-aware receipt helper are clear. The cursor format is an unversioned bare tuple and receipt calls are repeated across route handlers.

operations.reason: Queries are bounded and database clients are generally released in finally blocks. No performance, Worker, or operational failure checks were run for this review.

findings.description: BRD-07 cursor only carries position and card ID. listBoardCards accepts it without binding or comparing board ID, canonical filters, or a snapshot/structure revision. After a move changes ordering, a previously paged card can fall before the cursor and disappear from the remaining traversal instead of producing STALE_CURSOR. Cross-board/filter cursors are also accepted as raw seek points.
findings.counterevidence: The query remains scoped to the requested board and active cards, and ordering is deterministic by position then ID. These controls do not enforce stale cursor semantics or prevent omissions.
findings.remediation: Encode and validate board, normalized filters, and the relevant snapshot/order revision in the cursor; reject mismatched or stale continuation with 409 STALE_CURSOR and add mounted PostgreSQL regressions for reorder, board mismatch, and filter mismatch.

The frozen round-2 JSON requires additional full-check, Worker, API/contract, CRD and COM/DEL checks.

findings.remediation: Provide a test-safe database configuration that permits the specifically isolated stage2_boards database without broadening access to shared/live data, then execute frozen tests and add the missing receipt regressions.
